learning_outcomes.text: Foundation of knowledge through an interdisciplinary approach that combines Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics for understanding the properties of materials.
Understanding of the principles that correlate macroscopic properties of materials with different levels of material structure (atoms, bonds, crystal lattice).
Understanding the basic principles of experimental methods for the analysis of the structure and composition of matter.
Application of realistic basic design strategies and materials selection schemes through realistic design problems of materials design.
Knowledge of the basic methods of materials characterization and understanding in quantitative and qualitative terms the results of such measurements.
Can predict qualitatively and quantitatively, where possible, the macroscopic properties of materials based on their structure.
Be able to describe qualitatively and quantitatively the basic requirements a material should satisfy for use in a realistic application.
Can choose the most suitable material based on the specifications for applications involving mechanical, thermal or electrical properties or their combination.

syllabus_topics: Structure and constituents of atoms, Fundamentals of Quantum Mechanics, Quantum mechanical description of atoms
Forces between atoms, Potential, Ionic bonds, Ionization potential, Electron Affinity, Covalent bonds, Metallic bonds, Secondary Bonds, Wan der Waals bonds, Hydrogen bonds

Crystalline, amorphous materials, Unit cell, Atomic Packing Factor (APF), Metallic crystals, (FCC), (BCC), (HCP), Ionic solids, Covalent solids. Polymer structures, molecular configurations, co-polymers, polymer crystallinity. Crystal Lattice, Crystal systems, Crystallographic directions, Crystallographic planes, Structural analysis techniques, X-ray Diffraction (XRD)
Solubility limit, Phases, unit phase diagrams, binary phase diagrams, eutectic systems. Phase transformations: kinetics and equilibrium. Iron-carbon alloys.
Deformation, Mechanical Stress, Elastic behavior, Plastic behavior, Tensile strength, Ductility, Resilience, Toughness, Hardness.
Heat Capacity, Phonons, Thermal Expansion, Thermal conductivity, Thermal stress-resistance to thermal shock

Ohm’s law, electrical conductivity, Electrical properties at the atomic scale, Energy bands, Fermi energy, Carrier mobility and conductivity, Electrical properties of metals, Semiconductors, Ionic ceramics, Electrical properties of polymers, Conductive polymers
teaching_methods: Open and free educational material available through the eClass webpage (lecture slides, solved and unsolved exercises, simulations and animations, supplementary materials, video-recorded lectures, selected previous exams, useful links and examples, sets of self-evaluation tests)
Communication through email and constant office hours
assessment_rules: Student performance is evaluated through final written exams, which account for 100% of the grade. The evaluation criteria are accessible on the class webpage.
bibliography: W. D. Callister, “Materials Science and Engineering”, Willey (2001)
